title: D. MEX Replacement on Tree
statement:
You are given a tree rooted at 1 with n vertices and a permutation p of length n consisting of integers 0, 1, …, n - 1, where p_v represents the weight of vertex v.

Let S_v denote the set of weights written on the vertices belonging to the path from 1 to v. Define a function f as f(v) = MEX(S_v), that is, the MEX over the set consisting of the weights of vertices on the simple path between the root and v (inclusive), where MEX of a collection of integers c_1, c_2, …, c_k is defined as the smallest non-negative integer x which does not occur in the collection c.

Your goal is to find the maximum value of ∑limits_{v = 1}^n f(v) after performing the above operation no more than once (possibly zero).

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1 ≤ t ≤ 2·10^4). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5) — the number of vertices of the tree.

The second line of each test case contains n integers p_1, p_2, …, p_n (0 ≤ p_i ≤ n - 1) — the elements of array p. It is guaranteed that every integer from 0 to n - 1 appears exactly once in p.

Then n - 1 lines follow, each line contains two integers x_i and y_i (1 ≤ x_i, y_i ≤ n), indicating an edge between vertices x_i and y_i. It is guaranteed that these edges form a tree.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 2·10^5.

For each test case, output a single line containing an integer: the maximum value of ∑limits_{v = 1}^n f(v) after performing the above operation no more than once (possibly zero).
